finding: The constructed theory is feasible at canonical and across the BULK of every single O(1) prefactor's declared band, but it is feasible-but-MARGINAL, not robustly central. Of the engine's 11 knife-edge prefactors -- each with a declared factor-of-~2 ignorance band -- 5 are fully SLACK (the constructed point stays feasible across the whole band) and 6 are LOAD-BEARING (['anomaly_rho', 'bnossw_pref', 'cft_alpha', 'complexity_cmax', 'matter_s3_cm', 'scalar_wgc_beta']): pushing one of them to the ADVERSE EDGE of its declared band knocks the point just infeasible. Crucially, every break is an EDGE effect, never central -- the constructed point stays feasible across at least 78% of every prefactor's band (the worst case), and each load-bearing prefactor breaks only in the outer ~10-25% near one end, against a single named constraint (anomaly_rho->anomaly_inflow, bnossw_pref->BNOSSW monogamy, cft_alpha->CFT bound, complexity_cmax->complexity cutoff, matter_s3_cm->matter s^3 positivity, scalar_wgc_beta->scalar WGC). This is the honest meta-audit: the result does NOT rest on most O(1) conventions, but the constructed point is not deep in the interior either -- it sits close enough to ~6 constraint boundaries that an adverse O(1) excursion in any one reaches it. That is exactly what one expects of the Chebyshev CENTER of a tiny, ~3-dimensional, non-convex consistent+observed region (v2.333, v2.332): the center of a small region is necessarily close to many of its walls. It also generalizes and confirms v2.344 -- anomaly_rho is in the load-bearing set, breaking at its low edge exactly as predicted (the constructed parity 0.06 exceeds the anomaly budget near the rho=0.03 floor). The robust reading: a genuine feasible point, insensitive to O(1) ignorance across the bulk of every band, but marginal by construction -- its feasibility has ~78%+ headroom in each prefactor individually, not a fat interior cushion.
honest_scope: This is a one-at-a-time (OAT) sensitivity sweep: each prefactor is varied with all others held at canonical, so it does NOT capture JOINT excursions -- several prefactors at their adverse edges together would break feasibility more easily than any one alone, so the per-prefactor headroom here is an OPTIMISTIC (upper-bound) read of robustness; the constructed point is almost certainly more marginal under joint O(1) variation than the >=78%-per-band figure suggests. Feasibility is sampled on a 9-point grid per band, so a narrow infeasible sliver between grid points could be missed and the feasible sub-ranges are sampled, not proven. The bands are the engine's own declared factor-of-~2 conventions (PLAUSIBLE_RANGES), not published numbers, and the whole stack is the toy-basis encoding with the 4 data constraints (incl. the cosmic-birefringence hint, v2.329 caveat). 'Feasible' is a yes/no on the single constructed point -- it says nothing directly about the size of the feasible region (the marginality is INFERRED, consistent with the v2.333 ~3D tiny-region picture). Robust content: 5 of 11 prefactors are fully slack, the other 6 break only near one band edge against a named constraint, and the point is feasible across >=78% of every band individually. Toy basis. A meta-audit of the result's dependence on tunable conventions, reported with the OAT caveat.
